risks: No participants. The risk is a pathway designed around reports from well-resourced urban centres that fails distant or disadvantaged patients.
data: Published and publicly available material; local figures quoted in aggregate.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: place of residence (distance to infusion), language and socioeconomic position affect whether patients complete treatment before surgery. The review charts provisions for distant patients and interpreters, and the design discussion will weigh them explicitly.
effectiveness: Success is a pathway design the planning committee can adopt, with options for distant patients.
efficiency: Existing resident time and library support.
grants: None needed; an evaluation of the local pathway after launch could seek regional quality funding.
partnerships: Orthopaedic surgeons, pre-assessment nurses, a primary care representative and a patient partner who travelled for surgery.
rebPath: No research ethics review is needed for a scoping review of published and public material; a later evaluation of the local pathway would be screened by the research ethics board.
limitations: Reports may describe intended rather than actual pathways; limited reporting of times.
summary: No participants; equity centred on distance and language.
